scope: Explicit streaming-export terminal scan output only; fixed 4 MiB return pool. Full-buffer views, logical row counts, zero slack; ordinary query/cursor exact-size path unchanged. No stored format or wire-form change. Quiet-host Gate A outstanding.
fixture: 1048576 exported rows x200, 16 exported groups, 987 MiB OPFS in 17 groups including excluded hot group; 1 generated group copied to distinct addresses. Verification poison off, normal integrity checks on.
componentScope: 5 fresh-process alternating AB/BA rounds each campaign. Real ReturnPool and real two-way structuredClone transfer; caller rounds fresh/reused native storage; synthetic logical byte fills. Excludes setup/loading/warmup/GC, IO/decode/frame assembly/MessagePort latency. All physical slack is charged. RSS absolute loop peak includes allocator state left by variant warmup; loop growth uses post-warmup/GC baseline. Sampling every 256 events can miss shorter peaks. Bench reference policy compared with independent class enumeration in generated tests.
browserScope: Real ProtocolClient.exportStream, SQL/compose/server/executor/ResultSink/ResultChannel and real transfer/release. Fixture catalog/snapshot descriptors replace B3 discovery; excludes client row-object construction. Minimal request/hit counters included on both routes. Paired control uses current runtime with exact sizing, candidate with classes; pool contents and old capabilities cleared before EACH paired pass. Normal standalone retains the pool across five passes. Fixed campaign RSS baseline; no forced GC between passes. Raw outlier retained.

series.scope: one renderer and worker, space, governor and pool across five rounds (two queries per paired round); no forced GC between passes; collection only after campaign

safety: Fresh/reused capacities validated for safe size, >=logical bytes, and element alignment. Source ownership set, same result grant, declared exact capacity and full-buffer view checks required to adopt. Cached/page/dictionary/slab buffers never authorized. Physical byteLength participates in reservation, source ownership, frame credit and return pool cap. Returned buffers retain existing capability/provenance, detachment and size checks, are zeroed on reuse, and are never awaited. Trusted-client provenance limit unchanged.
